title: contact free noise cancelling headphone
abstract: A contact-free noise cancelling headphone that removes noise introduced into an open space from the outside is provided. The headphone includes a first microphone and a third microphone that are located outside when the headphone is worn and receive a primary noise signal contaminated by a feedback signal and a feedback interference signal, a first processing unit and a fourth processing unit that remove the feedback signal and the feedback interference signal from the contaminated signal, control filter characteristics, phase, and amplitude by frequency band for the extracted primary noise signal to generate an inverse-phase noise control signal, and output the inverse-phase noise control signal to a speaker, a second microphone and a fourth microphone that are located inside when the headphone is worn and receive a residual noise signal contaminated by an interference signal, a third processing unit and a sixth processing unit that remove the interference signal from the contaminated signal, extract the residual noise signal, and deliver the residual noise signal to a main controller, and the main controller that generates a control signal that controls filter characteristics, phase, and amplitude by frequency band so that an energy level of the residual noise signal becomes a minimum value and delivers the control signal to the first processing unit and the fourth processing unit, thereby effectively removing noise introduced into a noise removal space existing between the contact-free worn headphone and an ear.

title: hearing aid using artificial intelligiece
abstract: According to the present invention, a hearing aid using artificial intelligence includes two earplug bodies, each of which includes a microphone that converts a sound wave of ambient sound into an electrical signal to generate an ambient sound signal, a speaker that converts an electrical signal of sound into a sound wave, and a controller that processes the ambient sound signal to generate the electrical signal of sound. The controller includes an artificial intelligence sound analysis module that performs artificial intelligence analysis on the ambient sound signal to distinguish and separate a speech signal and a non-speech signal that is not the speech signal, and an output sound signal generation module that generates an output sound signal in which a volume of the speech signal output after being separated from the artificial intelligence sound analysis module is increased and a volume of the non-speech signal is decreased and delivers the output sound signal to the speaker.

title: urban air mobility noise reduction system and method
abstract: The present invention relates to an urban air mobility noise reduction system. The present invention includes an urban air mobility (UAM) that detects and provides RPM information and position coordinate information of a propeller, and a noise canceling device that receives actual noise generated when the UAM takes off or lands through a microphone provided at a mobility transfer station, calculates a canceling wave by using the actual noise generated from the UAM input through the microphone, and outputs the calculated canceling wave to the UAM through a plurality of speakers.

title: apparatus and method for controlling noise in collection of buildings, and noise processing apparatus
abstract: The present invention relates to a method for controlling noise in a collection of buildings and, in one aspect, includes inputting reference noise information from a reference sound collector located in a zone of the collection of buildings, generating a noise spatial map for the reference sound collector by using a position of the reference sound collector, the reference noise information, and information on the collection of buildings, and generating active noise information for canceling noise received by the collection of buildings by using position information of an active noise generator located in the zone of the collection of buildings and the noise spatial map. In another aspect, the present invention relates to an apparatus for controlling noise in a collection of buildings and includes a receiver that inputs reference noise information from a reference sound collector located in a zone of the collection of buildings, a map generator that generates a noise spatial map for the reference sound collector by using a position of the reference sound collector, the reference noise information, and information on the collection of buildings, and an active noise generator that generates active noise information for canceling noise received by the collection of buildings by using position information of an active noise generator located in the zone of the collection of buildings and the noise spatial map. In still another aspect, the present invention relates to an apparatus for processing noise in a collection of buildings and includes a reference sound collector located in a zone of the collection of buildings and generating reference noise information, an active noise generator located in the zone of the collection of buildings, and an active noise controller that inputs the reference noise information from the reference sound collector, generates a noise spatial map for the reference sound collector by using a position of the reference sound collector, the reference noise information, and information on the collection of buildings, and generates active noise information for canceling noise received by the collection of buildings by using position information of the active noise generator and the noise spatial map, the active noise generator generating active noise by receiving the active noise information from the active noise controller. Active noise control and processing in a collection of buildings according to the present invention enable active noise to be generated at an effective cost in the collection of buildings, thereby reducing inconvenience caused by various noises in the collection of buildings. In addition, since reference noise can be collected for a plurality of active noise generators by a small number of reference sound collectors, there is no need to install a reference sound collector for measuring noise for each active noise generator, thereby reducing installation, maintenance, and management costs of an active noise generation service. Furthermore, according to the present invention, an active noise control system can be installed and serviced for each collection of buildings, each complex of collections of buildings, or each zone or region, thereby performing an active noise information processing service at an efficient cost.

title: device and method for modeling secondary path for active noise cancelling of vehicle
abstract: A method and apparatus for modeling acoustic transfer characteristics of a secondary path for active noise cancelling are disclosed. According to one aspect of the present invention, the method includes outputting a predetermined signal through a speaker inside a vehicle and acquiring an error signal from a microphone inside the vehicle, generating an estimated error signal for a virtual microphone position corresponding to the microphone by using a virtual microphone filter capable of estimating an acoustic signal for the virtual microphone position corresponding to the microphone, extracting a secondary path signal for the predetermined signal transmitted from the speaker through a secondary path between the speaker and the virtual microphone position from the estimated error signal, and calculating a transfer function relating to acoustic transfer characteristics of the secondary path based on the secondary path signal.

title: apparatus and method for noise reduction
abstract: A noise reduction apparatus of the present invention includes a device communication unit that receives terminal location information from a mobile communication terminal, a direction control unit that rotates a microphone and a speaker in a direction of a location of the mobile communication terminal based on the terminal location information, a microphone that is rotated under control of the direction control unit and measures noise in the direction in which the mobile communication terminal is located, a canceling waveform generator that analyzes the measured noise and generates a canceling waveform having a phase opposite to that of the noise, and a speaker that is rotated under control of the direction control unit and outputs the canceling waveform in the direction in which the mobile communication terminal is located.

title: adaptation enhancement for a road noise cancellation system
abstract: A road noise cancellation (RNC) system may include a signal analysis controller for detecting non-stationary, transient events based on a sensor signal having spectral or temporal characteristics significantly different from steady-state road or cabin noise. When such a non-stationary event is detected, the RNC system may modify the signal to mask the non-stationary event so that an adaptive filter of the RNC system is not mis-adapted due to the transient, non-stationary event, or may slow or suspend adaptation of its controllable filter for a duration of a frame that includes the non-stationary event.

title: inter-floor notification type inter-floor noise prevention method
abstract: An inter-floor notification type inter-floor noise prevention method according to the present invention includes a plurality of accelerometers installed on a bottom surface of a floor slab of an upper-floor household, a noise analysis control device installed in a lower-floor household to store and analyze measurement values of the accelerometers, a sound receiving microphone unit coupled to the control device to measure noise generated in the lower-floor household due to a noise source generated in the upper-floor household, a wall pad for a home network coupled to the control device, and a central management control device connected to the wall pad. The control device analyzes acceleration data measured by the accelerometers and noise data measured by the sound receiving microphone unit and transmits a quantitative noise level to the central management control device through the wall pad. When the noise level is equal to or greater than a predetermined noise level, the central management control device sends a warning sound regarding noise generation to an upper-floor wall pad of the upper-floor household.

title: system and method for simulating noise environment of vehicle
abstract: A method and system for simulating a noise environment of a vehicle are disclosed. According to an aspect of the present invention, a simulation system for a noise environment of a vehicle includes a memory that stores reference signal samples and noise signal samples, a controller that generates a reference signal based on the reference signal samples, generates a noise signal based on the noise signal samples, and transmits the reference signal to a noise control system, and a speaker that converts the noise signal into a sound wave and outputs the sound wave.

title: noise cancelling system
abstract: An object of the present invention is to improve a noise canceling effect in a hybrid type noise canceling system. A noise canceling system according to an aspect of the present invention includes: an input unit that inputs a noise signal from a microphone that receives external noise; a digital section including an A/D conversion circuit that converts the noise signal into a digital signal, a digital filter circuit that filters the digital signal, and a D/A conversion circuit that converts the filtered digital signal into a first noise canceling signal as an analog signal; an analog section that outputs a second noise canceling signal obtained by filtering the noise signal; a synthesis unit that outputs a third noise canceling signal obtained by synthesizing the first noise canceling signal and the second noise canceling signal; an output unit that outputs an output signal obtained by adding the third noise canceling signal to a voice signal from a sound source; and a feedback unit that feeds back a control signal based on the first noise canceling signal and the second noise canceling signal to the analog section.

title: system and method for simulating noise environment of vehicle
abstract: A method and system for simulating a noise environment of a vehicle are disclosed. According to an aspect of the present invention, a simulation system for a noise environment of a vehicle includes a memory that stores reference signal samples and noise signal samples, a controller that generates a reference signal based on the reference signal samples, generates a noise signal based on the noise signal samples, and transmits the reference signal to a noise control system, and a speaker that converts the noise signal into a sound wave and outputs the sound wave.

title: device and method for controlling divergence of noise control system of vehicle
abstract: A device and method for controlling divergence of a noise control system of a vehicle are disclosed. According to an aspect of the present invention, in a computer-implemented method for controlling divergence of a noise control system of a vehicle, first filter coefficients of an adaptive filter and second filter coefficients updated from the first filter coefficients are received, a first parameter representing a difference between the first filter coefficients and preset reference filter coefficients and a second parameter representing a difference between the second filter coefficients and the reference filter coefficients are calculated, and the adaptive filter is updated based on a comparison between the first parameter and the second parameter.

title: adaptive noise control system with improved robustness
abstract: A method for determining an estimate of a secondary path transfer characteristic in an ANC system is described. According to an example of the present invention, the method includes positioning a microphone array in a listening room symmetrically with respect to a target listening position and reproducing at least one test signal by using loudspeakers arranged in the listening room to generate an acoustic signal. The acoustic signal is measured by microphones of the microphone array to obtain microphone signals from each microphone of the microphone array, and a numerical representation of the secondary path transfer characteristic is calculated for each microphone signal based on the test signal and each microphone signal. The method further includes averaging the calculated numerical representations of the secondary path transfer characteristic to obtain an estimate of the secondary path transfer characteristic to be used in the ANC system.

title: feedforward active noise control
abstract: Sound reduction includes receiving a reference signal corresponding to undesired sound present in a target space and generating a cancel signal representing the undesired sound present in the target space based on the reference signal. Sound reduction further includes generating sound that destructively interferes with the undesired sound present in the target space based on the cancel signal and delaying at least one of the reference signal and the cancel signal to reduce or compensate for a runtime difference between signal paths that deliver the reference signal to the target space.

title: a hearing protection device based on the intelligent active noise control
abstract: The present invention relates to a hearing protection device based on intelligent active noise control and includes: a first microphone which is located outside an ear when the hearing protection device is worn and receives an external noise signal; a speaker provided inside the hearing protection device and outputting a reverse phase signal of the noise signal to the inside of the ear; and an inverse-phase signal generator that receives the noise signal from the first microphone, filters the noise signal, phase-controls the filtered noise signal to generate a reverse phase signal, and filters the noise signal to block a frequency band of a preset communication pattern. With the hearing protection device, external warning sounds or voices can be filtered and passed or amplified so that external sound sources necessary for work other than noise can be heard to smoothly perform work.

title: active noise control platform system and active noise control method using the same
abstract: The present invention relates to an active noise control platform system and a noise control method using the same, and includes a microphone that detects noise, a speaker that outputs a sound source, and a control device that receives a noise control algorithm, receives noise control condition information, and outputs a sound source that cancels noise through the speaker. Various algorithms for active noise control can be applied through the system, enabling efficient noise control.

title: active noise control apparatus and method of controlling the same
abstract: The present invention relates to a vehicle active noise control apparatus and control method capable of protecting privacy by making it difficult for one passenger in a vehicle to hear another passenger's voice. In a vehicle active noise control method according to an embodiment of the present invention, a masking sound signal is generated based on a first microphone signal input through a reference microphone corresponding to a first seat, and the masking sound signal is output through a headrest speaker of a second seat. In generating the masking sound signal, a first transfer function corresponding to an acoustic transfer path between the headrest speaker and the reference microphone is applied to the masking sound signal to generate an expected howling input signal, the expected howling input signal is subtracted from the microphone signal to generate a second microphone signal, and the masking sound signal is generated based on the second microphone signal.

title: method and system for vehicle active noise control system
abstract: Disclosed are a method and system for active noise control of a vehicle. In one embodiment, the method performs ANC (Active Noise Control) to reduce noise flowing from the outside to the inside of the vehicle and received by a microphone, determines whether a level of residual noise of reduced noise by the ANC is greater than a threshold, and, if the level of the residual noise is greater than the threshold, performs re-measurement of a secondary path model when the vehicle is turned off.

title: stored secondary path accuracy verification for vehicle-based active noise control systems
abstract: An active noise cancellation (ANC) system includes facilities for verifying the accuracy of modeled transfer characteristics stored in secondary path filters that provide estimation of a secondary path, that is, a transfer function between a speaker and an error microphone. A signal analysis controller uses estimated anti-noise or music signals to adjust an error signal from the error microphone and can detect ANC instability or noise boosting. Such noise boosting can indicate that stored transfer characteristics in the secondary path filters do not accurately represent an actual secondary path, and upon detection of noise boosting, the stored transfer characteristics of the secondary path filters may be modified.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM FOR ROAD USE AND PROCESSING METHOD THEREOF
abstract: The present invention relates to an artificial intelligence-based active noise control system for road use and a processing method thereof. The road active noise control system of the present invention comprises a plurality of microphones and a plurality of speakers installed in a multi- and multi-layer structure on a moving path of a vehicle and an active noise control device for active noise control. The active noise control device uses artificial intelligence-based deep learning technology to analyze detected noise and noise signals and extract and generate an inverse phase wave signal for removing and cancelling the noise and the noise signals, outputting the same to a speaker to remove or reduce the noise and the noise signals. Therefore, according to the present invention, when noise and noise signals are generated during the driving of a vehicle, an optimized anti-phase processed wave signal corresponding to the noise and the noise signal is extracted and generated in reaction thereto at an ultra-high speed through deep learning iterative learning and is outputted, thereby quickly and precisely removing or reducing the noise and the noise signals generated on a large scale and continuously around the road of the vehicle.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2025

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM FOR RAILWAYS AND PROCESSING METHOD THEREOF
abstract: The present invention relates to an artificial intelligence-based active noise control system for railways and a processing method thereof. In the active noise control system for railways of the present invention, a plurality of microphones and a plurality of speakers are installed in a multi- and multi-layer structure on a moving path of a railway vehicle, and an active noise control control device for active noise control analyzes detected noise and noise signals using artificial intelligence-based deep learning technology to extract and generate an inverse phase wave signal for removing and canceling noise and noise signals, and outputs the same to a speaker to remove or reduce the noise. Therefore, according to the present invention, when noise occurs during the operation and movement of the railway vehicle, an optimized anti-phase processed wave signal corresponding to the noise and noise signal is extracted and generated in reaction thereto at an ultra-high speed through deep learning iterative learning and is outputted to a directional speaker, thereby rapidly and precisely removing or reducing the noise generated on a large scale and continuously from a large linear structure of transportation.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2025

title: FEEDBACK ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL METHOD FOR HEADPHONE OR EARPHONE AND ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL METHOD THEREBY
abstract: The present invention relates to a feedback active noise control method for a headphone or an earphone, and more particularly, to a feedback active noise control method for a headphone or an earphone and an active noise control system thereby, to enable the processing of noise introduced from the outside to the headphone or the earphone in real time. The feedback active noise control method for a headphone or an earphone and the active noise control system thereby process an introduced noise signal by approximating a finite impulse response filter of a low order which is frequency-warped based on the constrained optimization of a feedback method by an infinite impulse response method, in the active noise control method for actively controlling the noise signal introduced from the outside.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2018

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL APPARATUS FOR REDUCING NOISE IN CONSTRUCTION SITE
abstract: According to one aspect of the present invention, provided is an active noise control apparatus including an active noise control unit for reducing a noise in a construction site. The active noise control unit comprises: a first microphone for measuring the noise; a holder with adjustable height; and a speaker installed in the holder and radiating an offset noise with a phase opposite to the noise in the noise source direction in accordance with the noise measured from the first microphone so as to offset the noise. Moreover, a plurality of active noise control units are installed to be spaced from each other along a boundary of the construction site.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2018

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL TYPE HEARING PROTECTION METHOD AND DEVICE THEREFOR
abstract: The present invention relates to a hearing protection device and a method thereof to clearly transmit the voice of a user to the other user even when a hearing protector is worn. The hearing protection device according to an embodiment of the present invention comprises: a receiver; a microphone unit; an active noise control unit; a noise reduction unit; and a control unit. The receiver receives a signal through an external network. The microphone unit acquires an audio signal around a user. The active noise control unit receives the signal from the receiver and the microphone unit, generates a signal canceling out a noise signal directly transmitted to the ear of the user by using the noise signal included in the surrounding audio signal, and removes the directly transmitted noise signal. The noise reduction unit receives the audio signal acquired from the microphone unit, redistributes the energy of the audio signal, and increases the recognition rate of a voice signal among the voice signal and the noise signal included in the audio signal. The control unit determines a communication mode and a face-to-face mode according to the selection of the user, activates the active noise control unit when the communication mode is selected, and activates the noise reduction unit when the face-to-face mode is selected.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2017

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL PLATFORM SYSTEM AND NOISE CONTROL METHOD USING SAME
abstract: The present invention relates to an active noise control platform system and a noise control method using the same. The active noise control platform system comprises: a microphone for sensing noise; a speaker for outputting a sound source; and a controller for setting a noise control algorithm and receiving noise control condition information to output a sound source canceling noise through a speaker, thereby enabling the noise to be efficiently controlled since the system can apply various algorithms for active noise control.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2017

title: VEHICLE CALL SYSTEM BASED ON ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL AND METHOD THEREOF
abstract: Disclosed is a vehicle call method based on active noise control. The method comprises the steps of: activating a plurality of active noise cancellation (ANC) microphones provided in a vehicle to respectively correspond to locations of occupants; classifying a talker primarily based on a talker tone for a received voice signal of a counterpart as a call is connected with the counterpart; classifying the talker secondarily by receiving a voice signal of the occupant in the vehicle which is output through a speaker in the vehicle, through the ANC microphone; matching the speaker positioned at the location of the occupant corresponding to the talker with each occupant as the classification of the talker is completed; and reproducing a call voice through the matched speaker. The present invention transmits the speaker voice in three dimensions.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2024

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL APPARATUS FOR VEHICLE AND CONTROL METHOD THEREOF
abstract: The present invention relates to an active noise control apparatus for a vehicle, capable of protecting privacy by making it difficult for one occupant to hear a voice of another occupant in the vehicle, and a control method thereof. The active noise control method of the vehicle according to one embodiment of the present invention comprises the steps of: firstly determining a noise level based on a first microphone signal input through a microphone corresponding to a first seat; secondarily determining whether or not a masking sound signal generated based on the first microphone signal is output and a size based on the noise level and a level of the first microphone signal; and outputting the masking sound signal through a headrest speaker of a second seat in response to the second determination.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2023

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL DEVICE FOR VEHICLE AND CONTROLLING METHOD THEREOF
abstract: The present invention relates to an active noise control device for a vehicle and a controlling method thereof, wherein privacy can be protected by preventing a passenger from hearing the voice of another passenger easily in a vehicle. The active noise control method for a vehicle according to an embodiment of the present invention comprises the steps of: generating masking audio signals based on first microphone signals inputted through a reference microphone corresponding to a first seat; and outputting the masking audio signals through a headrest speaker of a second seat. The generating step may include the steps of: generating expected howling input signals by applying, to the masking audio signals, a first transmission function corresponding to an audio transmission path between the headrest speaker and the reference microphone; generating second microphone signals by subtracting the expected howling input signals from the microphone signals; and generating the masking audio signals based on the second microphone signals.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2023

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROLLER
abstract: In accordance with the present invention, provided is an active noise controller comprising: a plurality of speakers (100) installed within a predetermined radius from a noise source; a plurality of microphones (200) installed within a predetermined radius from the noise source; a control part (300) controlling the operation of the speakers (100) and the microphones (200); amplitude calculation parts (400)(400) calculating an amplitude value by analyzing a noise inputted from the plurality of microphones (200); and a signal processing part (500) generating a virtual control sound source based on the calculated amplitude value, and outputting the generated virtual control sound source through the plurality of speakers (100). The sound source outputted from the speakers (100) is a masking sound for canceling the noise inputted from the plurality of microphones (200). Therethrough, the active noise controller of the present invention can bring about an advantage of suppressing a noise generated from a spindle noise generation part of a machine tool.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2022

title: HEARING PROTECTION DEVICE BASED ON INTELLIGENT ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL
abstract: The present invention relates to a hearing protection device based on intelligent active noise control, which comprises: a first microphone placed at an external side of an ear when wearing the hearing protection device to receive a noise signal from the outside; a speaker provided at an internal side of the hearing protection device, and outputting an antiphase signal of the noise signal to an internal side of the ear; and an antiphase signal generating unit receiving the noise signal from the first microphone to be filtered, phase controlling the filtered noise signal to generate an antiphase signal, and filtering and blocking a frequency band of a communication pattern that is set in advance. As stated above, according to the hearing protection device, as a warning sound at the outside or a voice is filtered to pass or be amplified, an external sound source necessary for work except for noise can be heard to smoothly perform the work.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2018

title: NOISE REDUCING DEVICE AND NOISE REDUCING METHOD USING ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL
abstract: According to one embodiment of the present invention, a noise reducing device using active noise control comprises: a main body installed to be attached to and detached from a portion of a human body within a predetermined distance from an ear of a user; a plurality of microphone sensors installed in the main body and measuring a noise generated from a noise source; a processor installed in the main body and generating a control sound signal having the same size with and an opposite phase to a noise signal transmitted from the noise source by using an active noise control algorithm; and a plurality of speakers installed in the main body and outputting a control sound to reduce the noise by using the control sound signal.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2016

title: METHOD AND DEVICE FOR CONTROLLING NOISE IN COMPLEX BUILDING AND NOISE TREATING DEVICE
abstract: The present invention relates to a method for controlling noise in a complex building. According to an aspect of the present invention, the method for controlling noise in a complex building includes: a step of receiving reference noise information from a reference noise collector positioned in a section of the complex building; a step of generating a noise space map on the reference noise collector by using a position on the reference noise collector, the reference noise information, and information on the complex building; and a step of generating active noise information offsetting the noise which the complex building receives, by using the position information of an active noise generator positioned in the section of the complex building and the noise space map. Also, according to the other aspect of the present invention, a device for controlling noise in a complex building includes: a receipt unit receiving the reference noise information from the reference noise collector positioned in the section of the complex building; a map generating unit generating the noise space map on the reference noise collector; and an active noise generating unit generating active noise information offsetting the noise which the complex building receives. According to the present invention, active noise control and treatment in the complex building enable the active noise to be generated at efficient costs in the complex building and can reduce inconvenience due to various noise in the complex building.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2017

title: IN-VEHICLE SOUND CONTROL DEVICE AND CONTROL METHOD THEREOF
abstract: The purpose of the present invention is to provide an active noise control method and device for improving the performance of active noise control by considering the relationship between noise control signals and audio signals, the characteristics of noise signals, the characteristics of speakers, etc. An in-vehicle sound control device and a control method thereof are disclosed. According to one aspect of the present disclosure, a method for controlling an in-vehicle sound control device is provided, which comprises a step of obtaining at least one of a reference signal of an accelerometer or an error signal obtained from a microphone sound signal; a step of estimating a road surface environment corresponding to the road surface on which a vehicle is traveling using the reference signal; and a step of adjusting a gain to generate a noise control signal having a size within a preset range using at least one of the road surface environment and the error signal.  COPYRIGHT KIPO 2024

abstract: A device comprising: an acoustic metamaterial (AMM), wherein the phase velocity of an acoustic wave is reduced at low frequencies as compared to the phase velocity at higher frequencies; a microphone array (MIC) of at least two microphones (mic1, mic2) embedded in the acoustic metamaterial (AMM) and configured to detect acoustic waves.

title: APPARATUS AND METHOD FOR AN ACTIVE AND PROGRAMMABLE ACOUSTIC METAMATERIAL
abstract: An acoustic metamaterial (1400) including cells (1402) to digitally process an incoming sound waveform (1404), and to produce a corresponding response sound waveform (1406) as a function of a frequency and a phase of the incoming sound waveform, to produce a total response sound waveform (1408) that, when combined with the incoming sound waveform, modifies the incoming sound waveform.

abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of acoustic metamaterials, in particular to a refrigerator, an acoustic metamaterial noise reduction device and a method for designing an acoustic metamaterial structure. title: Semi-automatic film acoustic metamaterial capable of regulating and controlling sound insulation peak frequency
abstract: The invention provides a semi-automatic film acoustic metamaterial capable of regulating and controlling sound insulation peak frequency. title: ACOUSTIC METAMATERIAL NOISE CONTROL METHOD AND APPARATUS FOR DUCTED SYSTEMS
abstract: An acoustic metamaterial noise control system of embodiments of the disclosed technology combines acoustic metamaterial principles with absorptive materials, with a result of a significant reduction in sound radiation within, or emanating from, an HVAC duct. Sound waves that impinge on the noise control system placed at the end (terminal opening of an air duct to ambient space within a room/building), or at a predetermined place on the duct, cause the sound waves to reflect back to the start of the noise control system and also to be absorbed by sound waves within the absorptive core. abstract: Abstract : ABSTRACT A SYSTEM OF ACOUSTIC METAMATERIAL BASED HEARING AID FOR TACKLING TINNITUS AND URBAN NOISE MITIGATION The present invention discloses a system (20) for acoustic metamaterial based hearing aid for eliminating the challenges faced by the people due to tinnitus and urban noise. abstract: The invention discloses an air conditioner noise monitoring method, device and system and an air conditioner, and belongs to the field of noise monitoring. title: MITIGATION OF MALICIOUS SONIC ATTACKS ON VOICE-BASED COMPUTING DEVICES
abstract: An acoustic filter mitigates audio signal-based attacks (particularly inaudible attacks in the ultrasonic frequency range) on voice-based computing devices by modulating the signals before they reach the device's microphone. One filter is formed as a rigid body defining multiple holes that exhibit local resonance phenomena that suppress incoming audio waves at specific frequencies. The filter distorts or otherwise modifies the attack signals and thereby prevents the microphone(s) from receiving the intended attack signal, and prevents the associated computing device from processing and executing the intended malicious "command"/signal. The filter can be tuned to be operable outside the frequency range of normal spoken commands, so that typical voice-based commands are unaffected by the filter. A frame is provided to enable one or more filters to be retrofitted to existing consumer electronics devices, outside their housings. Alternatively, new consumer electronics may be manufactured to include such filters inside their housings.

title: Signal shielding and sound insulating gadgets storing device
abstract: A storage device is configured for electromagnetic shielding and sound insulation to secure gadgets like phones and smartwatches in environments requiring cybersecurity or confidentiality. The device features a housing made from materials that block sound and electromagnetic interference comprising multiple compartments that detect stored gadgets via sensors. It employs passive acoustic insulation and active audio jamming to disrupt microphone functionality and prevent voice recognition. The compartments are adjustable, allowing different sliding or rotational configurations, and are equipped with locking mechanisms. A user interface provides real-time status updates, such as power state, compartment occupancy, and jamming activity. This multifunctional design ensures optimal protection of sensitive information during confidential meetings or in secure IT environments.

title: Methods, systems, apparatuses, and devices for facilitating stress adaption in a workstation
abstract: Disclosed herein is a system for facilitating stress adaption in a workstation. Accordingly, the system may include microphones disposed on the workstation. Further, the one or more microphones may be configured for generating first sound signals of first sounds associated with an environment of the workstation. Further, the system may include a processing device communicatively coupled with the microphones. Further, the processing device may be configured for analyzing the first sound signals, determining first sound characteristics of the first sounds, determining second sound characteristics of second sounds, and generating second sound signals for the one or more second sounds. Further, the system may include acoustic devices disposed on the workstation. Further, the acoustic devices may be communicatively coupled with the processing device. Further, the acoustic devices may be configured for emitting the second sounds based on the second sound signals. Further, the second sounds destructively interfere with the first sounds.

title: FLEXIBLE CONDUCTIVE HEARING AIDS
abstract: A flexible conductive hearing aid, comprises: (i) a flexible substrate, (ii) components, on or in the flexible substrate, including (a) a microphone, configured to produce an electrical signal from sound, (b) electronic circuits, connected to the microphone, configured to amplifying the electrical signal, (c) an actuator, connected to the electronic circuits, configures to produce vibrations in the flexible substrate from the amplified electrical signal, and (d) a power source, connected to the microphone and the electrical circuits. Furthermore, the flexible conductive hearing aid comprise (iii) optionally, a flexible top layer, on the components, and (iv) optionally, a flexible bottom layer, wherein the flexible substrate is on the flexible bottom layer.

title: IN-EAR HEADPHONE DEVICE WITH ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL
abstract: An in-ear headphone device for insertion in an ear canal of a person. The in-ear headphone device comprises a noise microphone, a loudspeaker and a signal processor arranged to provide an active noise control signal on the basis of a recorded audio signal from said noise microphone, wherein said loudspeaker is arranged to reproduce said active noise control signal in said ear canal. Further, the device comprises a damped vent comprising one or more vent elements and one or more dampening elements, said damped vent being arranged to couple said ear canal to an external acoustic environment. The damped vent is characterized by an inward vent transfer function HVI from said external acoustic environment to said ear canal. The damped vent is arranged to dampen an acoustic resonance of said one or more vent elements such that a resonance magnitude of said inward vent transfer function HVI of said damped vent in a resonance frequency range from 100Hz to 2kHz is maximally 3dB greater than a reference magnitude of said inward vent transfer function HVI in a reference frequency range from 20Hz to 100Hz.

title: AN ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: An active noise control system and a method of active noise control are disclosed. The active noise control system comprises an adaptive filtering module and a loudspeaker communicatively coupled to the adaptive filtering module. The adaptive filtering module is configured to compute estimated disturbance signals, time-dependent filtered reference signals and estimated power gains of a secondary path based on a Modified Filtered Least Mean Square (MFxLMS) model, to generate time-dependent variable penalty factors and to update a set of filter coefficients of an adaptive control filter of the MFxLMS model to compute a derivative term in a recursive-adaptive model of the adaptive control filter and to obtain an output set of the control signals. The active noise control system computes a variable penalty factor in real time based on a predefined maximum control signal output power to prevent an output of the system from saturating.

title: AUTOMATED ATTENTION HANDLING IN ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEMS BASED ON LINGUISTIC NAME EMBEDDING
abstract: Automated attention handling techniques are described herein for use with wearable audio components with active noise control (ANC) to suppress ambient sound. A name embedding model is trained automatically to convert name audio samples into linguistically distinct name classifications and/or unified audio samples. The name embedding model is used to generate reference embeddings for each of a user-enrolled set of names, and a relation network and a false rejection network are also trained. In real-time operation, the name embedding model converts real-time audio samples to real-time embeddings, the relation network compared the real-time embeddings to the reference embeddings to look for candidate matches, and the false rejection network validates the candidate matches to detect when one of the user-enrolled names has been invoked. Detecting such an invocation automatically triggers the ANC to switch to a conversation mode.

title: ACTIVE AERODYNAMIC NOISE CONTROL APPARATUS AND METHOD
abstract: An active aerodynamic noise control apparatus includes a SoundCam installed inside a vehicle, an aerodynamic noise data measurement unit configured to measure aerodynamic noise data, an ultrasonic data measurement unit configured to measure primary ultrasonic data, an acoustic data measurement unit configured to measure primary acoustic data, a correlation coefficient calculation unit configured to calculate a correlation coefficient, an ultrasonic sensor location confirmation unit configured to confirm a secondary ultrasonic sensor location, an ultrasonic data collection unit configured to collect secondary ultrasonic data, an acoustic data collection unit configured to collect secondary acoustic data, an aerodynamic noise region determination unit configured to determine an aerodynamic noise region, an active noise control sound generation unit configured to generate an active noise control sound, and an active noise control sound output unit configured to output the generated active noise control sound.

title: HEARING DEVICE WITH ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL
abstract: According to the invention, a hearing device (earphone, 'hearable', earbud, earplug, hearing aid, etc.) with a moving coil speaker and with an active noise control circuit has at least one hole in the speaker membrane (41) and/or, if present, in another element of the partition between the speaker front side and the speaker back side to which the membrane (41) belongs. Such other element of the partition may for example be a membrane frame (43) surrounding the membrane and connecting it to a housing (40) of the hearing device. The speaker back side is coupled to ambience, for example via at least one rear port (52).

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: An active noise control system includes an error adder that generates an error signal by adding an output of a left-seat left microphone and an output of a left-seat right microphone, an adaptive filter that generates a noise canceling sound from a reference signal by performing an adaptive operation using the reference signal and the error signal, a left channel gain adjustment section that adjusts a gain of the noise canceling sound to be output to a left-seat left speaker, and a right channel gain adjustment section that adjusts a gain of the noise canceling sound to be output to the left-seat right speaker. A ratio between the gains of the left channel gain adjustment section and the right channel gain adjustment section matches a ratio between loudness levels of noise transmitted to the output of the left-seat left microphone and the output of the left-seat right microphone.

title: STORED SECONDARY PATH ACCURACY VERIFICATION FOR VEHICLE-BASED ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEMS
abstract: An active noise cancellation (ANC) system may include provisions for validating the accuracy of a modeled transfer characteristic stored in secondary path filters, which provides an estimate of the secondary path (i.e., the transfer function between a speaker and an error microphone). Using estimated anti-noise or music signals to adjust an error signal from the error microphone, a signal analysis controller may detect ANC instability or noise boosting. Such noise boosting may indicate the stored transfer characteristic in the secondary path filter does not accurately represent the actual secondary path. According, upon detection of noise boosting, the stored transfer characteristic of the secondary path filters may be modified.

title: SEMI-ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM FOR AN AIRCRAFT
abstract: A semi-active noise control system (100) comprising a layer (110) that is configured to be part of an interior panel of an aircraft (200) is disclosed. The layer (110) comprises a plurality of conductive tracks (111), a driver arrangement (112), a plurality of tuned mass dampers (113), and a plurality of sensors (114). Each of the plurality of tuned mass dampers (113) comprises an eigenfrequency that depends on a control signal applied to the tuned mass damper (113) and is connected to the driver arrangement (112) via at least one of the plurality of conductive tracks (111) and configured to receive control signals from the driver arrangement (112). Each of the plurality of sensors (114) is connected to the driver arrangement (112) via at least one of the plurality of conductive tracks (111) and is configured to sense vibrations and/or acoustic sounds and send measurement signals (115) to the driver arrangement (112). The driver arrangement (112) is configured to analyze the measurement signals (115) and to generate and send control signals (116) to the tuned mass dampers (113) such that the eigenfrequency of the tuned mass dampers (113) is matched with the frequency of the vibrations and/or acoustic sounds sensed by the sensors (114).

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: An active noise control system includes circuitry configured to perform independent component analysis when a level of a sound output from a microphone becomes greater than a predetermined level. In an independent component analysis process, by the independent component analysis, the circuitry separates a noise component from monitoring sound data that is output from the microphone, and stores data representing the noise component as statistical noise data. An adaptive filter in the active noise control system performs an adaptive operation to adapt an output of the microphone as an error, and outputs, as a noise cancellation sound from a speaker, a sound represented by noise cancellation sound data that is obtained by filtering the stored statistical noise data. The adaptive filter adapts, as an error, a filter coefficient used in filtering the monitoring sound data output from the microphone.

title: METHOD FOR GENERATING AN IMPERCEPTIBLE STIMULUS SIGNAL FOR ON-LINE SECONDARY PATH FOR AUTOMOTIVE ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEMS
abstract: A system and method for generating a stimulus signal as a solution for an adaptive secondary path component of an active noise cancellation (ANC) system having at least one audio signal source to provide an audio signal in a cabin of the vehicle, a shaped noise generator provides a shaped-noise signal in the cabin of the vehicle, at least one controller programmed to activate the shaped noise generator and add the shaped noise signal to the audio signal to generate a stimulus signal, and at least one loudspeaker to project the stimulus signal within the cabin of the vehicle for the ANC system to generate an anti-noise signal.

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: There is provided an active noise control system (1) for canceling noise without being easily affected by the displacement of a user. A first cancellation signal output from a first speaker (12) cancels noise at a first cancellation point (41), which is a standard position of the right ear of a user, together with a second cancellation signal output from a second speaker (14). In addition, the second cancellation signal output from the second speaker (14) cancels noise at a second cancellation point (42), which is a standard position of the left ear of the user, together with the first cancellation signal output from the first speaker (12). The first speaker (12) and the second speaker (14) are arranged side by side on a second line segment, which passes through the midpoint of a first line segment connecting the first cancellation point (41) and the second cancellation point (42) to each other and is perpendicular to the first line segment, and a range (400) where the relationship between noise and the first cancellation signal and the second cancellation signal is the same as that at the cancellation point is extended.

title: METHOD AND SYSTEM FOR SELECTING SENSOR LOCATIONS ON A VEHICLE FOR ACTIVE ROAD NOISE CONTROL
abstract: The present disclosure provides a method for determining an arrangement of reference sensors for active road noise control (ARNC) in a vehicle by means of an automatic calibration system, wherein the method comprises: mounting a plurality of vibrational sensors on a plurality of structure elements of the vehicle to generate a plurality of vibrational input signals; mounting at least one microphone inside a cabin of the vehicle to capture at least one acoustic input signal; and determining the arrangement of reference sensors from the plurality of vibrational sensors by determining a subset of vibrational sensors which sense the main mechanical inputs of road noise contributing to the at least one acoustic input signal.

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: Provided is an "active noise control system and an in-vehicle system" to cancel noise at a plurality of seats using a single microphone (9). A first seat noise control device (3) corrects sound collected by a microphone (9) to sound at a listening position of a sound of a user seated on a first seat, generates a cancel sound that cancels, at the first seat, the sound of a second seat audio source (2) output from a second seat speaker (8) by using an adaptive filter that receives the sound of the second seat audio source (2) with the sound as an error, and outputs the cancel sound from a first seat speaker (7). A second seat noise control device (4) corrects the sound collected by the microphone (9) to sound at the listening position of the user seated on the second seat, generates a cancel sound that cancels, at the second seat, the sound of a first seat audio source (1) output from the first seat speaker (7) using an adaptive filter that receives the sound of the first seat audio source (1) with the sound as an error, and outputs the cancel sound from the second seat speaker (8).

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: To provide an "active noise control system" capable of satisfactorily canceling noise even when a position of an ear fluctuates. Adaptive operations of a first noise control system (1) and a second noise control system (2) including a speaker that outputs noise cancellation sound, a microphone that detects an error signal, an auxiliary filter that generates, from a noise signal, a correction signal that corrects the error signal so that a difference in a position between the microphone and a noise cancellation position is compensated, and an adaptive filter that performs an adaptive operation using the corrected error signal to generate the noise cancellation sound from the noise signal are alternately performed. A transfer function learned in a state in which the second noise control system (2) is stopped is set in the auxiliary filter of the first noise control system (1), and a transfer function learned in a state in which the adaptive operation of the first noise control system (1) is stopped is set in the auxiliary filter of the second noise control system (2).

title: ACTIVE ROAD NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM WITH OVERLOAD DETECTION OF PRIMARY SENSE SIGNAL
abstract: An active road noise control includes generating with a sensor arrangement a primary sense signal representative of accelerations, motions and/or vibrations that occur at a first position on a vehicle body, and providing a noise reducing signal by processing the primary sense signal according to an adaptive mode of operation or a non-adaptive mode of operation. It includes generating within the vehicle body noise reducing sound at the second position from the noise reducing signal, and evaluating the primary sense signal and controlling the processing of the primary sense signal so that the primary sense signal is processed in the adaptive mode of operation when the magnitude of the primary sense signal undercuts a first threshold and in the non-adaptive mode of operation when the magnitude of the primary sense signal exceeds a second threshold, the first threshold being equal to or smaller than the second threshold.

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM, SETTING METHOD OF ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM, AUTOMOBILE, AND AUDIO SYSTEM
abstract: Provided are "an active noise control system (1), a setting method of the active noise control system (1), and an audio system (3)" that cancel a plurality of noises. Two subsystems, each including a microphone (12, 14), a speaker (13, 15), a canceling sound-generating adder (1118, 1128), an error-computing adder (1117, 1127), and two adaptive filters W (1113 and 1114, 1123 and 1124, 1115 and 1116, 1125 and 1126) and two auxiliary filters H (1111, 1121, 1112, 1122) that ACCEPT two noises as input, are provided in correspondence with two cancellation positions. Each canceling sound-generating adder (1118, 1128) adds together the outputs from the adaptive filters (1113 and 1114, 1123 and 1124, 1115 and 1116, 1125 and 1126) and outputs the result to the speaker (13, 15) of each subsystem. Each error-computing adder (1117, 1127) adds together the output from the microphone (12, 14) of the subsystem and the output from the auxiliary filter (1111, 1121, 1112, 1122) of the subsystem, and the result is treated as the error of the adaptive filters (1113 and 1114, 1123 and 1124, 1115 and 1116, 1125 and 1126) of each subsystem. A transfer function is learned in advance and set in each auxiliary filter (1111, 1121, 1112, 1122) such that each error computed by each error-computing adder (1117, 1127) becomes 0 when a transfer function in which each noise is canceled at each cancellation position in a predetermined standard acoustic environment is set in each adaptive filter (1113 and 1114, 1123 and 1124, 1115 and 1116, 1125 and 1126).

title: ACTIVE ROAD NOISE CONTROL
abstract: An active road noise control system method for a vehicle includes picking up noise at a multiplicity of positions in or on the vehicle and generating a multiplicity of noise sense signals representative of road noise originating from a road noise source in or at the vehicle, and processing, according to a beamforming scheme, the multiplicity of noise sense signals to generate a reference signal and to provide a sensitivity characteristic for picking up the noise that comprises one main lobe directed to the road noise source. The system and method further includes iteratively and adaptively processing the reference signal to provide a noise reducing signal, and generating at one or more positions in an interior of the vehicle, from the noise reducing signal, noise reducing sound at a listening position in the interior of the vehicle.

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL MICROPHONE ARRAY
abstract: An apparatus and method are presented for an active noise control system with a selector mechanism to select an appropriate reference signal for an active noise control algorithm responsive to several noise sources, some of which generate may sounds intermittently.

title: ADAPTIVE MODELING OF SECONDARY PATH IN AN ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: The technology described herein can be embodied in a computer implemented method that includes detecting, by one or more processing devices, onset of an unstable condition in an active noise control system. The method also includes obtaining, responsive to detecting the onset of the unstable condition, updated filter coefficients for a system-identification filter configured to represent a transfer function of a secondary path of the active noise control system. The updated filter coefficients are generated using a set of multiple subband adaptive filters, wherein filter coefficients of each subband adaptive filter in the set are configured to adapt to changes in a corresponding portion of a frequency range associated with potential unstable conditions in the active noise control system. The method also includes programming the system identification filter with the updated coefficients to affect operation of the active noise control system.

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM AND ON-VEHICLE AUDIO SYSTEM
abstract: There is provided an "active noise control system and an on-vehicle audio system" which are most suitable for acoustic control in a vehicle and adapt to a change in a transfer function. Audio (noise source) is output as a cancellation sound through a variable filter (151) and a first filter (154) and transmitted to the second filter (155), a subtractor (156) subtracts an output of a second filter (155) from an output of a microphone (16), and an adaptive algorithm execution unit (152) updates a transfer function of the variable filter (151) so that the subtracted result becomes 0. A transfer function A for the first filter (154) is a transfer function which can cancel noise at a position of a user's ear by setting, as the cancellation sound, a sound obtained by applying the transfer function A to audio at the time of learning, and a transfer function B for the second filter (155) is a transfer function which can eliminate, for the cancellation sound, a difference between a sound obtained by applying the transfer function B to audio and the output of the microphone (16).

title: MITIGATION OF UNSTABLE CONDITIONS IN AN ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL SYSTEM
abstract: The technology described in this document can be embodied in a computer-implemented method that includes receiving a portion of a feedback signal of an active noise control (ANC) system, and processing the portion of the feedback signal using an adaptive line enhancer (ALE) filter to detect a tonal signature. The method also includes determining, by one or more processing devices, that the tonal signature represents an unstable condition, and responsive to determining that the tonal signature represents an unstable condition, generating one or more control signals for adjusting one or more parameters of the ANC system, to mitigate the unstable condition.

title: HEARING DEVICE WITH ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL BASED ON WIND NOISE
abstract: A method for operating a hearing device including a component to be worn at least partially in an ear of a user and an active noise control (ANC) system is provided. The method includes capturing an audio with a microphone system, generating an audio signal based on the captured audio, and generating a feed-forward (FF) compensating signal based on the captured audio. The method includes monitoring the acoustic environment of the hearing device for presence of wind noise, and mixing the audio signal with the generated FF compensating signal at a ratio dependent on whether wind noise is detected to provide an acoustic output signal. A hearing device including an active noise control (ANC) system and a wind noise monitor is also provided.

title: ACTIVE NOISE CANCELLING SYSTEM, BASED ON A FREQUENCY DOMAIN AUDIO CONTROL UNIT, AND RESPECTIVE METHOD OF OPERATION
abstract: The present application describes an active noise cancelling system, operating in a frequency domain architecture. In particular, the system now proposed is based on an audio control unit (1), comprising at least one digital transducer (5), to acquire an error signal (9) from an error channel (8), and quadrature module (2) to perform the reconstitution of said error signal in the frequency domain. The active noise cancelling system further comprises electroacoustic transducers (7.1) that are used to emit the reconstituted sound, outputted by the audio control unit, to the environment, in order to cancel the unwanted noise (14). The present application also describes a method for operating the system developed. By performing the noise cancellation in the frequency domain allows decreasing the latency associated with the acquisition process, which in turn improves the noise cancelation algorithm performance. The overall hardware complexity of the acquisition process is also reduced.

title: ACTIVE NOISE CONTROL HEADPHONES
abstract: Embodiments of active noise control (ANC) headphones and operating methods thereof are disclosed herein. In one example, a headphone for ANC includes a speaker, an internal microphone, a processor, and a filter function module. The speaker is configured to play an audio based on a first audio source signal. The internal microphone is configured to obtain a mixed audio signal comprising a noise signal and a second audio source signal based on the audio of interest played by the speaker. The processor is configured to determine a current system parameter of the ANC headphone based on the mixed audio signal at a first time point and determine a current parameter of a filter function module based on the current system parameter of the ANC headphone and pre-tested data. The filter function module is to perform ANC based on the determined current parameter of the filter function module.

title: Mitigation of unstable conditions in an active noise control system
abstract: The technology described in this document can be embodied in a computer-implemented method that includes receiving a portion of a feedback signal of an active noise control (ANC) system, and processing the portion of the feedback signal using an adaptive line enhancer (ALE) filter to detect a tonal signature. The method also includes determining, by one or more processing devices, that the tonal signature represents an unstable condition, and responsive to determining that the tonal signature represents an unstable condition, generating one or more control signals for adjusting one or more parameters of the ANC system, to mitigate the unstable condition.

According to the system, a filter based on the variable step LMS algorithm is applied to identification of a secondary channel; a filter weight value is updated by adjusting a step value of the filter; in order to obtain a relatively fast convergence rate, the step value of self-adaptive filtering in an initial phase is relatively high; and when the self-adaptive filtering approaches a steady state, the step size is reduced, so a relatively low steady state error can be obtained. abstract: A sound is detected and a reference signal (x) is generated. A sound is detected and a specific signal (j) is generated. A first speaker (10A) emits a first sound wave. The control device (110) implements active noise control by causing the first speaker (10A) to emit the first sound wave on the basis of the reference signal (x) and the control filter (CF1).

The ANC module unit includes an ANC housing shaped to fit within the air intake or exhaust an ANC core configured to be secured within the ANC housing which includes a microphone configured to detect a sound generated by the power generation unit a control board configured to control the noise canceling sound based on the sound signal from the microphone and a set of pre determined noise reduction transfer functions and a first speaker configured to deliver a first noise canceling sound to the air intake or exhaust. The at least one first filter generates at least one first filter output, wherein each of the at least one first filter has at least one non-static filter and at least one static filter connected in a series fashion. In which, at least one noise collecting system is adopted for collecting a real environmental noise so as to generate a reference signal and a target signal. Subsequently, according to the reference signal and the target signal, a first adaptive system identifying unit is enabled to complete a first system identification process for producing a first adaptive filter.
